newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds see-sawed late in the session on Friday, initially taking a knock from U.S. employment data and turning negative before rallying into the close to end largely flat.

The market was motionless at higher levels through most of the day, waiting for March U.S. payrolls numbers, but a strong hourly earnings component of the report rapidly led Treasuries lower, with European asset markets quick to follow.
A late Bund future rally, however, was enough to lift the Dutch market back to parity at the end of the session, though dealers said conditions would stay difficult next week.

The rise of 0.4 percent in average hourly earnings, more than expected, had been enough to suggest wage pressures still building in the U.S., one said, and might solidify expectations for a fresh interest rate rise there in May.
Dutch data on Thursday showing inflation forecast at 2.75 percent in 1997 had also been bearish news for the local bond market, he said.
But another dealer said the tight second quarter supply in the local market would continue to be supportive. Only one new issue is planned in the quarter.
Spreads to Germany narrowed slightly during the day, as Guilders continued to underperform. Some analysts see the 10-year yield discount more than halving in the short term.
The recent steepening trend also continued, with the 10-two year spread pushing out to 234 basis points from 220 a week ago.
